key_insight: There is no universally best flow surrogate: the right architecture depends on whether the dynamics are boundary-driven or self-sustained, with time handling being the deciding factor.
engineering_relevance: For process and fluid simulations, surrogate selection should match the physics and validation should use failure-mode-specific metrics rather than pointwise RMSE alone.
method: Compared 8 surrogate architectures across two transient flow regimes: CMP slurry film and cylinder wake (Karman vortex street).
Varied representation style (full-field vs latent) and rollout style (one-shot vs autoregressive/stepwise).
Evaluated models with five physical criteria: field accuracy, structure, invented motion, amplitude, and timing.
evidence_signal: A one-shot full-field model reached 3.2% relative error on cumulative wall shear stress in CMP, while an autoregressive latent DeepONet preserved 96% of wake shedding power that other models nearly eliminated.
watch_item: Offline training cost matters: the surrogate only pays off after enough queries, so deployment value depends on the number of post-training evaluations and the regime-specific setup.
paper_title: No Free Lunch in Flow Surrogates under Time-Varying Boundary Conditions: A Two-Regime Study
